label: The two surfaces cap comment quantity at different numbers and the universal contract has none: Webflow says 'Maximum 5 comments per 10 lines of code' (cross-language-rules.md:47, repeated in javascript/quick-reference.md:68) while OpenCode says three (naming-and-commenting.md:170 plus twelve more files), and the universal guide defines comment policy by purpose with no count. Both thresholds are surface rules over the same shared contract and neither cites a surface reason, so the same file shape is judged differently depending on route. Reproducing case: rg -n 'comments per 10' .skilled/skills/sk-code prints the Webflow rows at 5 and the OpenCode rows at 3 in one output. NEW P2.

The relative link labels in surface shared-tier files are stale pre-move paths even where targets resolve: cross-language-rules.md:173 labels a link '../../universal/code-style-guide.md' over target '../../../shared/references/universal/code-style-guide.md', and the OpenCode naming file does the same over a four-level target at line 235. With enforcement.md:310 (iteration 4) the label-drift class now has four instances across three files, enough for one sweep rather than four fixes. Reproducing case: rg -n '\[../../universal/code-style-guide' .skilled/skills/sk-code prints both labels; neither label path exists from the containing file's directory. NEW P2.

Verified single-sourced and non-contradicting: the two structure rules (no double-underscore folder names, tests under a tests/ tree) appear only in the universal guide and have no surface copies to drift; the OpenCode surface's P0 restatements (boundary validation, secrets) add language examples while agreeing with the universal P0 list. ALREADY-ADOPTED, no action.

Part 1 override inventory closes with exactly two rule-level divergences: the comment-quantity thresholds (5 vs 3, no universal owner) and the unowned-budget orientation filed in iteration 4. Every other scanned surface shared-tier rule either defers to the universal tier by explicit pointer (cross-language-rules.md:31) or adds surface-specific rules the universal tier never reaches. Closing statement; no further Part 1 iteration planned unless a later iteration reopens it. NEW P2.
